summary: Configured 1 GB of zstd-compressed zram swap on node1 via zram-generator, active at boot with swap-priority=100 (higher than any disk-backed swap), verified persistence across a full node reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected baseline: no swap configured, zram-generator not installed
Installed zram-generator and zram-generator-defaults via dnf
Wrote /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf with zram-size=1024, compression-algorithm=zstd, swap-priority=100, fs-type=swap

Discovered and corrected a stale zram0 device created from package defaults (lzo-rle, ~1.7G) by swapoff + resetting /sys/block/zram0/reset + daemon-reload before re-running the setup service so the custom config took effect
Started systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service and dev-zram0.swap, verified 1G zstd swap active with priority 100
Confirmed dev-zram0.swap is WantedBy=swap.target (auto-activated by the generator each boot) and /etc/fstab has no disk-backed swap to conflict
Captured baseline boot_id, triggered systemctl reboot on node1, polled until reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed
Re-verified post-reboot that zram swap (1G, zstd, priority 100) came back active automatically

evidence.requirement: At least 512MB of compressed in-memory swap configured
evidence.summary: Baseline showed 0 swap and no zram-generator; package installed and config written specifying 1024MB zstd zram swap

evidence.requirement: Swap is compressed (zstd) and correctly sized after fixing initial default-config mismatch
evidence.summary: After resetting the stale default zram0 device and re-running setup, zramctl/swapon show /dev/zram0 as 1G zstd-compressed swap active with priority 100
fstab has no disk swap entries; dev-zram0.swap carries priority 100 (systemd default disk swap priority is -2/lower), and unit is WantedBy=swap.target

Captured baseline boot_id d052eb57..., issued systemctl reboot (acknowledged before disconnect), polled through connection failures, confirmed new boot_id 95c8ae0a... proving an actual restart, then verified zram swap (1G zstd, priority 100) was automatically active again post-boot
